findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is convoluted, always returns false, and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` followed by `if enabled { return false }; return false` returns false on every path. The `sqlExpressions` toggle therefore has no effect, and the function reads as if it gates on the flag. The inverted `!` and the identical branches will confuse the next maintainer and invite a mistaken 'fix' that re-enables the path. The call also dereferences `h.features`, which the SQL branch did not do before, so a reader built with nil features would now panic on any SQL query. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions, return the error unconditionally with a clear comment and drop the helper and the feature-toggle lookup.

findings.title: Misleading error and stale flag semantics when SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: A user who enables the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle gets `sqlExpressions is not implemented` for any SQL expression. The toggle's registry description and docs still say it enables SQL expressions, and the frontend can still offer the option. The behavior (deliberately disabled for a security fix) and the user-facing message are inconsistent. The flag's description or docs should be updated to say it is disabled, or the message should say SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: No tests added or updated for the disabled SQL expression behavior
findings.body: The PR touches no test files. `sql.TablesList` and `NewSQLCommand` now always fail because the stub `RunCommands` returns 'not implemented'. Any existing test that expects a successful `TablesList` or `NewSQLCommand` (for example `parser_test.go` or `sql_command_test.go`) will fail or must be removed, and none are updated here. There is also no test that `ReadQuery` rejects `QueryTypeSQL`, or that the `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path fails closed. For a security fix, a regression test that SQL expressions cannot be created or executed is warranted.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path gives a generic, misleading error
findings.body: The `UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` path has no explicit check for SQL being disabled. It fails closed only because the stub `RunCommands` errors inside `TablesList`. The caller then sees `error reading SQL command` (a bad-request about invalid SQL), and the real reason is only in server logs at Warn/Error level. Security depends on a side effect of the stub rather than an explicit guard. Users will think their query is malformed, and the log noise from the failing `json_serialize_sql` call is repeated on every attempt.

findings.title: Dead DuckDB-specific parsing code left behind
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('...')` command and parses the AST JSON, and `SQLCommand.Execute` is still wired to the stub DB. All of this is unreachable now that `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` always return 'not implemented'. It keeps the string-concatenated SQL construction around, which was part of the vulnerable pattern, and implies a working feature to readers. The unused paths, and the `jeremywohl/flatten` dependency that supports them, should be removed or clearly marked as disabled.
